overview: This concurrent resolution, which needed approval from both the House and Senate, allowed Emancipation Hall in the Capitol Visitor Center to be used on June 24, 2026, for a ceremony dedicating the Semiquincentennial Congressional Time Capsule. The time capsule honors the 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence. Preparations for the event had to follow conditions set by the Architect of the Capitol, the office that manages the Capitol buildings and grounds. Measures like this are the routine way Congress approves special events in Capitol spaces. Both chambers approved it, with the House notified of Senate action on June 18, 2026.
for: Supporters say it lets Congress mark the nation's 250th anniversary with a fitting ceremony in the Capitol.
against: Critics say it is a routine, symbolic measure that does not change any law or spending.
